one_line_intent: On systems with a VIA southbridge, rewrite the legacy PCI Interrupt Line register of on-board VIA devices so PIC-mode interrupts are routed correctly.
generated_by: claude-opus-5-5 (in-session, same prompt contract as reason.py)

architecture_rationale.claim: VIA chipsets route interrupts via the PCI Interrupt Line register even though it is normally informational; if the BIOS did not program it, interrupts go to the wrong place, so the kernel rewrites it.

evidence.excerpt: we need to ensure that the IRQ line register which usually is not relevant for PCI cards, is actually written so that interrupts get sent to the right place

architecture_rationale.claim: Two-step design: a separate quirk first detects which VIA southbridge exists and records the on-board device slot range (via_vlink_dev_lo/hi); this ENABLE-phase quirk then only touches devices inside that range. This split exists because device lookup was not available when quirks ran.

evidence.excerpt: So I used a two-step quirk as is done for some other quirks already.  First we detect the VIA south bridges and set the right low and high device limits
